messages:
morgan: quick follow-up to the residency RFC — I sketched a more compact API that unifies staging/pinned pools into a single Residency abstraction. goal: simpler rollout for private/dedicated and fewer cross-pool edgecases.
ryan: curious — does unified mean one global allocator or just one interface with multiple backends?
sophie: +1 to single interface. implementation can keep separate backends (fastpath pinned, async staging). we need clear guarantees for latency-critical paths though.
morgan: exactly. interface only. backend choice is pluggable. main ops: reserve(size), admit(tenant, token), demote_hint(token), reclaim(token), query_residency(token).
ana: small nit — `admit` needs to be async-friendly for batch warmups. do we return a lease object?
morgan: yeah returning a lease token is the plan, something like:```python
lease = residency.admit(tenant, size)
if not lease.ready():
  fallback_to_cpu()
```
ryan: locking concern: what about fastpath for short-lived allocations (inference microbatches)? we can't have per-allocation slow path.
sophie: consider split fastpath: local thread-local cache that maps to Residency tokens, no global lock. only the admission path touches global structures.
leo: runtime metrics we need: p99 admit latency, fail-to-admit rate, demote frequency, and cross-tenant evict churn. these drive rollout thresholds.
morgan: agreed. rollout plan: shadow-mode for 2 weeks (metrics only), then canary with one pool in dedicated, then gradual traffic shift. if fail-to-admit > 0.5% revert.
nana: telemetry: include sample traces with seq_len, model, tenant, and last_touch to correlate fragmentation vs workload.
ryan: tradeoffs: unified interface means simpler code paths but bigger surface for backward compatibility. we should keep compatibility shims for older alloc APIs for one quarter.
sophie: API sketch quick proposal:```go
// Residency provides occupancy guarantees and demotion hooks
type Residency interface {
  Reserve(size int) (Reservation, error)
  Admit(ctx Context, res Reservation) (Lease, AdmissionResult)
  DemoteHint(lease Lease, score float32)
  Reclaim(lease Lease)
  Query(lease Lease) ResidencyInfo
}
```
morgan: thanks — that shape lets us implement tenant-scoped quotas and admission policies. also exposes demote hints for quality-aware decisions.
leo: can we add a simple cost-estimate in AdmissionResult (expected p99 increase if admitted to staging)? ops want automated routing fallback.
sophie: yeah AdmissionResult{ok bool, staging bool, est_p99_ms int} — keep it tiny.
nana: one more: fallback semantics for private deployments (no staging allowed). API should allow a backend-level policy toggle to enforce deny-on-staging.
morgan: good call. I'll update the RFC appendix with the interface and rollout checklist. plan to put a prototype in a branch for perf tests.
ryan: please include microbench for admit hotpath under small allocation burst (1–8kB) and large-kvcache loads. i'll run SLO tests.
nana: infra-bot: deployment scheduled: residency-prototype branch -> test-cluster at 02:00 UTC for canary perf run :rocket:
infra-bot: CI passed, smoke tests ok.
morgan: thanks all — will ping when branch is up. :thumbsup:
